segments.strap: HEARTBEAT NEWS
segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Fuel depots burn, Ukraine's grid goes dark, gas hits a crisis high
bullets: Saudi jets hit Houthi fuel depots; Aramco offices burn
Dutch gas at its highest since 2022
U.S. inflation report and big-bank profits

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Wednesday, October fourteenth.

Today: Saudi jets strike Houthi fuel depots while a Houthi strike sets fire to Aramco offices, Russia's overnight barrage leaves six hundred thousand Ukrainians without power, and European gas hits its highest price since twenty twenty-two.
Plus bank profits, a bug in an A.I. company's conference room, a Bitcoin turnaround, and a long list of quick hits. Let's go.

segments.strap: SAUDI JETS HIT HOUTHI FUEL DEPOTS; ARAMCO OFFICES ON FIRE
segments.headline: Saudi Arabia and the Houthis trade strikes

graphic.title: Fuel depots in Sanaa, fire at Aramco
bullets: Coalition hits al-Sabaha fuel depot, Sanaa
Fire at Aramco building in Dhahran; no casualties
Houthis threaten Riyadh airport and Aramco

lines.text: The Saudi-led coalition struck the Houthis' al-Sabaha fuel depot in Sanaa and fuel sites at Hodeidah, according to the B.B.C. It first warned people to evacuate. That is the first Sanaa evacuation order since the war resumed.

Houthi missiles and drones were intercepted over Riyadh. Fires broke out at an Aramco building in Dhahran, with no casualties reported. The A.P., citing regional officials, says a Houthi strike hit offices at Aramco's headquarters. The Saudi Energy Ministry described a limited fire in an administrative building.
The Houthi-run broadcaster and residents also reported new coalition airstrikes on Sanaa on Tuesday. The Houthis now threaten Riyadh's airport and Aramco sites.
Diplomacy is going the wrong way. Oman-hosted U.N. peace talks were reported suspended, according to the reporting the watch desk read. Those are press accounts, not confirmed by either government.

segments.strap: RIYADH AIRPORT SHUT THROUGH OCT 17; NEARLY ALL FLIGHTS CANCELLED
segments.headline: Riyadh airport still closed

graphic.title: King Khalid airport: closed to Oct 17
bullets: Closed by notice until 2100 GMT Oct 17
About 20 dead in a week of attacks
IndiGo out to Oct 17, Etihad to Oct 19

lines.text: Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport stays closed under a notice running to twenty-one hundred G.M.T. on October seventeenth. Effectively every flight is cancelled.
The toll is about twenty dead this week. On October tenth, a strike killed twelve and injured three hundred nine. On October eleventh, Terminal Four was hit.
IndiGo cancelled Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Medina service through October seventeenth. Etihad is out through October nineteenth.

segments.strap: RUSSIA'S BARRAGE LEAVES 600,000 UKRAINIANS WITHOUT POWER
segments.headline: Trump's energy ceasefire is fraying

graphic.title: Energy ceasefire: third night of strikes

lines.text: The energy ceasefire announced by President Trump is not holding. Russia's overnight missile and drone barrage left about six hundred thousand people without power in Ukraine, according to ABC News.
President Zelenskyy said Russian forces hit Ukraine's power grid and oil and gas sites for a third straight night, the A.P. reports.
Kyiv answered with roughly five hundred drones toward Moscow. Oil terminal tanks are burning near Rostov, and a refinery in the capital region was damaged. Those figures come from press reports.
Trump declined to blame Russia for the breaches and noted Ukraine hit sites the day before. The Kremlin still does not confirm any ceasefire. It says consultations are ongoing.

segments.strap: E.U. SANCTIONS 826 RUSSIAN FIRMS; SENATORS HIT RUSSIAN DIESEL DEAL
segments.headline: Sanctions fight

graphic.title: Largest E.U. Russia listing ever
bullets: Senators demand end to diesel license

lines.text: The European Union adopted its largest sanctions listing yet. Eight hundred twenty-six Russian military-industrial companies and seven hundred forty-three executives are on it, including firms in the North Caucasus.

In Washington, bipartisan members of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, including Senator Shaheen, formally demanded that President Trump rescind OFAC General License one thirty-five, which allows Russian-origin diesel.
They also want the sanctions on enablers, authorized by Congress, put into effect. Joe's translation: Europe is tightening, and Washington is arguing about whether to loosen.

segments.strap: SHIPS HIT AGAIN IN HORMUZ; TRAFFIC AT A TENTH OF NORMAL
segments.headline: Strait of Hormuz

graphic.title: Hormuz: 8 crossings a day, not 85
bullets: Container ship and tanker hit Oct 13
Zero LNG or LPG carriers in 7 days

lines.text: The U.K. maritime agency, UKMTO, logged new strikes in the Strait of Hormuz. A container ship and a tanker were each hit by unknown projectiles on October thirteenth.
Iran said a ship sank after hitting a mine in the strait. The A.P. had no independent confirmation of the sinking.
A live tracker, hormuz dot now, shows a seven-day average of eight point four crossings a day. Before the crisis it was eighty-four point eight. No gas carriers crossed in seven days.
Off Oman, the tanker Petro Dolphin was still burning after an October eleventh drone hit. Two Indian sailors are missing. Nine were rescued.

segments.strap: DUTCH GAS HITS HIGHEST SINCE 2022; BRENT ABOVE $106
segments.headline: Oil, gas and coal

lines.text: Prices for the thing that heats Europe went up again. Dutch front-month gas touched eighty-seven euros and forty-three cents a megawatt-hour, the highest since December twenty twenty-two. Qatar's force majeure on liquefied gas and the Hormuz bottleneck are the reasons given.
Oil: Brent is near one hundred six dollars a barrel and U.S. crude near ninety-five in early Asian trading, on Saudi-Houthi supply risk. Russian diesel relief is capping the rise.
Thermal coal at Newcastle settled at its fifty-two-week high, one hundred fifty-three dollars and ten cents.

segments.strap: CHINA FACTORY PRICES JUMP 5%; KOSPI DOWN SIX STRAIGHT DAYS
segments.headline: Asian markets

graphic.title: China: factory prices up 5%, consumer prices soft

lines.text: China's producer prices rose five point zero percent in September, the highest since June twenty twenty-two. Gasoline added about half a point. Consumer prices rose only nine-tenths of a percent, below forecasts.

South Korea's KOSPI closed at six thousand eight, down point four four percent. That is six straight losses. India's rupee firmed to ninety-four ninety-two per dollar, though foreign investors have sold Indian stocks twelve sessions running.
Japan's Nikkei barely moved, and the yen sits near one fifty-eight. The A.P. says global markets were mixed, with chip shares helping some and inflation and bond worries weighing on others.
The I.M.F.'s Kristalina Georgieva urged the U.S. and other rich countries to rein in debt, saying higher bond yields pressure global markets and poor countries.

segments.strap: MEMORY CHIP SELL-OFF CONTINUES ON AN UNVERIFIED CHINESE CLAIM
segments.headline: Memory chips

graphic.title: Memory chips: a claim moves markets
bullets: CXMT claims 4F² DDR5 by end of 2026
SK hynix down after Tuesday's 8.9% drop

lines.text: The memory-chip sell-off has a cause, and it is a claim. China's CXMT says it will launch server memory on a denser cell design by the end of this year, and that it will beat Samsung there.
There is no independent teardown or spec sheet. That is day six unverified.
SK hynix fell again after Tuesday's eight point nine percent drop. Kioxia fell thirteen point three percent in Tokyo, even as S&P raised its credit rating a notch. Micron lost four percent on Monday.

segments.strap: BIG BANKS REPORT; U.S. INFLATION NUMBER LANDS AT 8:30
segments.headline: Banks and the inflation report

graphic.title: Bank profits; U.S. CPI at 8:30 ET

lines.text: Banks first. JPMorgan reported a third-quarter profit of fifteen point three billion dollars, five dollars and fifty-seven cents a share. Citi's S.E.C. filing shows net income of five point two billion dollars, two dollars eighty-five a share, on revenue of twenty-three point eight billion.
The A.P. says bank executives voiced concern about rates and inflation. Bank of America reports this morning too.
Then the number everyone wants. The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases September inflation at eight-thirty Eastern. The watch desk filed before it, so we do not have the result.

The backdrop, per press reports: the Fed, under Chair Kevin Warsh, raised rates to three seventy-five to four percent on September sixteenth. The next decision is October twenty-eighth. A weak jobs report had cooled hike bets.

segments.strap: OPENAI ENGINEER ARRESTED OVER ALLEGED BUG IN CONFERENCE ROOM
segments.headline: A.I. and the data center race

graphic.title: A.I.: a bug, a funding round, a data center
bullets: OpenAI engineer charged over recording device
OpenAI: no sign weights or data taken
NTT Data in talks on Anthropic Osaka site

lines.text: An OpenAI engineer was arrested and charged over an alleged attempt to record conversations in an executive conference room, the A.P. reports. The complaint says a device was found. OpenAI says it saw no sign that model weights, source code or customer data were taken.

Money. DeepSeek's second funding round doubled to one hundred billion yuan, about fourteen billion dollars, at an unchanged valuation of about five hundred billion yuan. That is a press report. The same reporting says it is preparing a stock-market listing.

And Nikkei reports NTT Data is in final talks to build Anthropic's first dedicated data center in Japan, in Osaka. Up to one trillion yen, five hundred megawatts, partial operation from twenty twenty-eight. Not yet signed.

segments.strap: CHARACTER.AI FILES CHAPTER 11; DISNEY AFFILIATE BIDS $20 MILLION
segments.headline: Character.AI files for bankruptcy

graphic.title: Character.AI: Chapter 11 and a Disney bid

lines.text: Character Technologies, the company behind Character dot A.I., filed for voluntary Chapter Eleven and announced a sale process. The platform keeps running.
A Disney affiliate is the stalking-horse bidder, offering twenty million dollars for a nonexclusive license to the company's intellectual property.
Elsewhere in business, TechCrunch reports Doug Field is now president of Mind Robotics, the industrial A.I. venture Rivian created. Rivian holds a minority stake.

segments.strap: BITCOIN E.T.F.s SNAP OUTFLOW STREAK WITH $175.7M INFLOW
segments.headline: Crypto

graphic.title: Bitcoin funds take in $175.7M
bullets: UK court: Chinese law governs 61,000 BTC claims

lines.text: U.S. spot Bitcoin funds took in one hundred seventy-five point seven million dollars on October thirteenth, according to Farside. Fidelity's fund took in one hundred three million, BlackRock's sixty-six. Monday had a sixty-five million outflow. Ether funds also had a first inflow day, twenty-four point eight million.
Bitcoin is near eighty-three thousand two hundred dollars, up one point six percent. Ether is near twenty-five twenty.
In London, the High Court ruled Chinese law governs fraud victims' claims on sixty-one thousand seized bitcoin, about five billion dollars. Lawyers are appealing.
Binance will shut its mining pool, cloud mining and transaction accelerator on November tenth, ending a six-year run.

segments.strap: LEDGER IMPLANT DRAIN: ABOUT $86M TAKEN; SALES HALTED IN GERMANY
segments.headline: Ledger tampered devices

graphic.title: Ledger: implants steal seed phrases
bullets: Sends it over an LTE eSIM

lines.text: Ledger's security team published its analysis of the implant found in tampered wallets. It reads the device screen, decodes the twenty-four-word recovery phrase, and sends it out over a cellular connection.

About eighty-six million dollars has been drained from Ledger users. Tether froze ten million dollars of its stablecoin tied to the theft. The German chains MediaMarkt and Saturn halted Ledger sales on October thirteenth.
CoinStats puts crypto thefts at two point six eight billion dollars through September, and ninety-eight million so far in October.

segments.strap: HURRICANE SIMON NEAR MEXICO; TS TRUDY FORMS; ISAIAS AFTERMATH
segments.headline: Storms across the hemisphere

graphic.title: Simon, Trudy, Isaias, Koguma
bullets: Isaias: at least 4 dead, outages as of Oct 10

lines.text: The National Hurricane Center places Hurricane Simon near nineteen point eight north, one hundred seven point nine west, with ninety-knot winds. Tropical Storm Trudy is near eleven north, ninety-nine west, with forty-five-knot winds.

Isaias aftermath, press reports as of October tenth: at least four deaths, with some outlets confirming only two. Outages that day were about four hundred twenty thousand in Florida and one hundred ninety thousand in Alabama. We found no final toll.

Across the Pacific, Typhoon Koguma is racing northeast away from Japan and weakening. In the Philippines, Kanlaon volcano is at Alert Level Two, with ash emission since the October tenth eruption and a four-kilometer exclusion zone.

segments.strap: APPEALS COURT HEARS D.C. GUARD CASE; FEDS SEARCH REP. OMAR'S HOME
segments.headline: Washington

graphic.title: Washington: courts and a search warrant
bullets: Appeals court hears National Guard case
Supreme Court takes D.O.G.E. records case
Trump campaigns in Alaska; midterms Nov 3

lines.text: A federal appeals court hears arguments today over President Trump's deployment of National Guard members to Washington. The city says it is unlawful domestic law enforcement.
The A.P. also reports federal agents searched Representative Ilhan Omar's Washington-area home under a judicially authorized warrant. The Justice Department gave no details.
The Supreme Court agreed to hear a watchdog's suit seeking public records on Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency.
And the president is flying to Alaska to campaign for Republicans. Midterms are November third.

segments.strap: EBOLA: 8,978 CASES IN CONGO; CHINA ISSUES PLAGUE ADVISORY
segments.headline: Health watch

graphic.title: Bundibugyo Ebola and a plague advisory
bullets: Kenya: one imported case, no new case since Oct 6

lines.text: Europe's disease agency counts eight thousand nine hundred seventy-eight Ebola cases and four thousand three hundred thirty-six deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo as of October eleventh. It is the second-largest Bundibugyo outbreak on record.
The C.D.C. says Kenya still has one case, imported, and one death. No new case since October sixth. A hundred twenty-two contacts were traced. Kenya's health ministry says no lockdown.

Separately, China issued a public plague advisory in Hulunbuir, Inner Mongolia, citing cross-border risk after a lab worker died at an institute in Irkutsk, Russia. The cause there remains officially pneumonia of undetermined cause. Plague is not confirmed.

segments.strap: YANDEX CLOUD STILL DOWN AFTER DRONE STRIKES; GITHUB ATTACK GROWS
segments.headline: Cyber and outages

graphic.title: Yandex outage; GhostAction campaign
bullets: 3 Yandex data centers hit by drones, Oct 8-11

lines.text: Ukrainian drone strikes damaged three Yandex data centers, El País reports. Die Welt says more than eighty Yandex Cloud services are out, and bot traffic has dropped sharply.
The Verge reports Russian bot networks are still active anyway. That is its view; the watch desk could not read the article.

Meanwhile the GhostAction campaign keeps spreading. Security firm Socket says more than five hundred GitHub accounts were hijacked and tens of thousands of repositories injected with workflows that steal cloud and A.I. keys.

segments.strap: PAKISTAN EMERGENCY IN KP; KOREA SAYS RATE HIKE COMING
segments.headline: World politics

graphic.title: Pakistan, Korea, Japan, India
bullets: Pakistan: emergency proclaimed in KP; protesters tear-gassed
Korea: President Lee says rate hike 'almost certain'
Delhi sit-in against election chief: day six

lines.text: From the First Light desk. Pakistan's National Assembly and Senate met in special sessions on the emergency proclaimed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. India Today reports tear gas and live rounds were fired at protesters.
In South Korea, President Lee said a rate hike cannot be avoided. The Bank of Korea's governor said policy stays restrictive at a three percent base rate.
Japan's Prime Minister Takaichi vowed continued backing for the International Criminal Court amid a feud with U.S. sanctions.
In Delhi, a sit-in against the chief election commissioner is in its sixth day. Three detained organizers are still held. The Supreme Court pushed the protest pleas to October fifteenth.

segments.strap: CHINESE COURT SENTENCES 3 TO DEATH IN MYANMAR SCAM-CENTER CASE
segments.headline: Death sentences in scam-center case

graphic.title: Fujian court: three death sentences
bullets: Wei family syndicate from Myanmar's Kokang

lines.text: A court in Fujian, China, sentenced three members of the Wei family scam syndicate from Myanmar's Kokang region to death, including Wei Huairen. It also handed down three life terms and fifty-five prison terms, according to CBS News.
In Seoul, regulators blocked twenty-seven unregistered foreign crypto exchange sites, including KuCoin and MEXC, and referred forty-four operators to investigators.

segments.strap: JAPAN'S MARS-MOON SAMPLE MISSION SET FOR OCT 20; INDIA'S LAUNCH SLIPS
segments.headline: Launch watch

lines.text: Japan's mission to bring back samples from Mars' moon Phobos is reconfirmed for October twentieth at four forty-one a.m. Japan time, from Tanegashima. Backup dates run to November seventh.
India's G.S.L.V. F-eighteen navigation satellite did not launch as hoped. Trackers now point to October fifteenth through twentieth. ISRO has not confirmed a date.

segments.strap: 'OTHER MOMMY' OPENS #1 WITH $27.5M; CHIIKAWA TOPS JAPAN A 12TH WEEKEND
segments.headline: Box office

lines.text: At the U.S. box office, 'Other Mommy' opened at number one with twenty-seven point five million dollars from thirty-three hundred theaters. 'Verity' fell sixty-four percent to eleven point five million. 'The Social Reckoning' opened with five point five million, and The Verge called it a flop.

In Japan, 'Chiikawa the Movie' was number one for a twelfth straight weekend, about seventeen point nine five billion yen. In China, 'Resident Evil: Outbreak Night' has made two hundred ninety-one million yuan.

segments.strap: ALSO TODAY
segments.headline: Also today

lines.text: India's HCLTech posted a record quarterly profit of fifty-one hundred thirty-two crore rupees, up twenty-one percent.

Federal regulators are looking into reports of Tesla robotaxis speeding in school zones, The Verge says. Shopify is opening its catalog to more A.I. shopping agents. Xbox is embracing A.I.-powered game ports.
Sydney home values are seven point one percent below their February peak, a sixth straight monthly fall nationally, press data says.
China's September car sales fell: retail down twenty-eight percent by one Reuters count, though exports rose seventy-three percent and electric cars hit a record sixty-seven percent share.

Nigeria's state oil company extended its sixty-six naira per liter petrol discount to October thirty-first. Nigeria's national grid collapsed again, the fourth major disruption this year, though the report is undated.

The F.D.A. approved forty-four novel drugs from January through September, against thirty-two a year earlier. And Chief Justice Roberts stayed an appeals court ruling in F.C.C. versus Sherrod Brown on October eighth. We found no outcome.

segments.strap: NLCS GAME 3 TONIGHT: BREWERS LEAD DODGERS 2-0; OHTANI LINEUP IN DOUBT
segments.headline: Sports

graphic.title: NLCS Game 3, NHL, cricket, Japan
bullets: Brewers lead Dodgers 2-0; Game 3 at 8 ET
India vs West Indies 4th T20I tonight

lines.text: Baseball. Milwaukee leads Los Angeles two games to none in the National League Championship Series. Game Three is tonight at eight Eastern. MLB's preview cites a report that the Dodgers may consider benching Shohei Ohtani. No final lineup yet.
Hockey. Montreal at Washington at seven-thirty Eastern, Dallas at Colorado at eight-thirty.
Football. Press reports say Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Junior has a rib injury, with an M.R.I. Monday and no result found. Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson hurt an ankle.

Cricket. India meets the West Indies in the fourth twenty-over match in Hyderabad at seven p.m. local time. In Japan, both Climax Series final stages open today. In Asian soccer, Al Hilal beat Al Sadd two to nothing.
